dialogues.speaker: Davy
dialogues.text: Ah, everything is so fresh and clear out in the wild. I'm so much more inspired here...

dialogues.speaker: Davy
dialogues.text: My work will be far greater than the nonsense that woman comes out with!

dialogues.speaker: Davy
dialogues.text: You'll probably run into her if you go to Springvale... She's my ex-wife, Myweiss. A bard, just like me.

dialogues.speaker: Davy
dialogues.text: I'm convinced the only reason I ever looked her way is because I bashed my head when Stormterror attacked!

dialogues.speaker: Davy
dialogues.text: Can you believe they used to call us Mr. and Mrs. Lovebard? It's so nauseating now that I think back on it.

dialogues.speaker: Davy
dialogues.text: But the worst thing of all is her original compositions...

dialogues.speaker: Davy
dialogues.text: Well. After the divorce, she started using her compositions as a way of stirring up controversy... Pfft. I, for one, do not consider anything she writes to be true poetry.

dialogues.speaker: Davy
dialogues.text: She will do whatever it takes to smear my name... and that's when she was the irresponsible one who never contributed to the home!

dialogues.speaker: Davy
dialogues.text: For example, we had a clear agreement that we would take it in turns to do the cooking and the housework. But every time I got back from a performance, she was never there. So I ended up cooking all the meals and doing all the housework myself!

dialogues.speaker: Davy
dialogues.text: At least I understand now — love is a big old hoax!

dialogues.speaker: Davy
dialogues.text: Goodbye! Come and listen to my new ballad when it's ready — it's called the Manacles of Matrimony.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything of note nearby?

dialogues.speaker: Davy
dialogues.text: Hmm, nothing especially noteworthy for a traveler, I'd say. Not recently, anyway. ...Except for my singing, of course.
